summary: Many owners find it comfortable and well built, with strong edge support, and some report six to ten years without sagging. The most common problems are sagging or body impressions after a few years and a firm feel that causes back pain, especially for side sleepers. Many ended up returning it.

Reviews are split, but the largest group describes sagging or body impressions, often within two to four years, along with back pain. Many also found it too firm, and a number of owners mention a lingering chemical or wool smell. Some others report several comfortable, cool years, and warranty claims were often disputed.

Opinions vary widely by firmness. Many owners wake with back pain, and the medium and firm versions are often called too firm or slow to break in, while some say the foam softens and hammocks. Plenty of others call it their best bed and report it easing back pain, and a fair number returned it.

Most reviewers like the crisp, cool feel, and many report these sheets lasting years. The main downside is durability for some, with holes, rips or thinning within months to two years, and several say quality dropped on newer sets. A few found the fabric scratchy at first, though it softens with washing.

Many owners find it comfortable and cooler than foam, and several report two to five years without problems or relief of back pain. The main complaints are sagging or softening, and firmness that causes hip and back pain, with some units reportedly firmer than the store model. Suits those who want a firmer hybrid feel.

Most reviewers who keep it like it, especially the soft version, and many side sleepers report less hip and back pain. Complaints are that the soft feels like quicksand or too soft over time, plus back pain for some and heat for a few. Some needed weeks or months to adjust.

Most reviewers say these sheets are soft and last, with many reporting several years of use without holes. The main downsides are that a few sets tore early or felt thin or rough, and some say newer sets were not as good as earlier ones. A couple found the price high unless bought on sale.

Reviews lean negative on durability. Many reviewers report holes, torn seams or fitted sheet corners within about a year, and some found the linen thin, pilling or stiff. Customer service was mixed on replacements. A smaller group says it lasted years and gets softer with washing.

Most reviewers are very happy with the original Purple, with many reporting six to ten years of comfortable, cool sleep and no sag. The main downside is sagging in the middle or where people lie, which some owners hit after two to six years, and warranty claims could take effort. Heavier owners often also like it.

Most reviewers find it comfortable, and several couples and heavier side sleepers love it. The main downside is heat, with some saying the cooling top does not help. Firmness is also hit or miss, with some finding it too firm and others too soft in the softer options.

Reviews are mixed. Several owners are happy with the cooling and long-term durability, particularly in the firm version. The most common complaint is that it feels too firm and takes weeks or months to break in, and a few report back pain or hip and shoulder aches for side sleepers. Some cite sagging.

Most owners praise the cooling and comfort and several report two years or more without problems. Downsides are some leaks and early failures, app or automatic temperature scheduling frustrations, and the high price. Support is often described as helpful, and some mention mismatched older hubs causing weaker cooling.

Reviews are split. Some call it comfortable and durable over several years, while others report firmness that causes shoulder and back pain, or the opposite problem of too soft. A few owners saw sagging or dips within one to two years, and some say it sleeps warm. Fit seems to depend on body weight.

Owners agree it cools very well, but reliability is the main concern, with leaks and units failing within one to two years the top complaint. Others cite poor WiFi and app problems, noise and a steep price. Some owners report years of trouble-free use, and support responses were mixed.

Mixed. The most common complaint is that the medium hybrid feels very firm, sometimes like concrete, and can cause back pain. Several say it still sleeps warm despite the cooling claims, though a few find it cool. Those who stick with it often praise the support and comfort after a break-in.

Most reviewers love it and describe it as comfortable, cool and supportive, with some calling it worth the price and a few taking it travelling. The main downside is that some pillows went flat after one to three years. A few found it too puffy or unsuitable.

Owners praise the cooling, but leaks are the dominant complaint, often after one to three years, and a few woke up to a soaked mattress. Replacement out of warranty was described as costly. Support was often quick when under warranty, and a few have had it work for two years without a problem.

Most reviewers find it comfortable and supportive, with several heavier sleepers and side sleepers praising it. The main downside is sagging or deep dips, which some reported within two years, sometimes with back and hip pain. Firmness choice matters, and a few found it warm or only fair at the edges.

Most reviewers find this weighted blanket breathable and cool, and several hot sleepers say it is the only weighted option they can use in summer. Complaints are few, including an odd smell on arrival and some fabric quality changes or pilling. Better suited to warm sleepers than those who want a snug feel.

Many long-term owners say it held up well, with several reporting seven to ten years of comfortable sleep. The downsides are that some found it too firm or hot, and a few developed sagging or back pain after four or more years. Reviews lean positive for side sleepers and couples.
